label: late-episode D1 after a1 S1 r then rare a1 S2 r; grows toward episode end
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (ep_trial - 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (tv("action", -3) == 2)
explanation: Very sparse feature (nonzero on 0.1% of steps), only at D1. It fires when the last trial was a rare a1->S2 rewarded trial and the trial before it was a1->S1 rewarded, and only in the last ~10 trials of the episode (ep_trial >= 90). Within that window its magnitude rises roughly linearly with ep_trial (about +0.04 per trial, up to ~0.5-0.7 near trial 98-99). It is much weaker (~0.02) after a1 S2 r late in the episode without the a1 S1 r trial before, and it is suppressed when the trial three back was an a2 choice. GO and D2 are always 0. Uses only observed trial history and episode time; the ideal-observer belief_lo adds nothing beyond history (the belief-decile table scores 0.00), so dropping model outputs costs nothing here: the profile reference scores give all observed 0.04 and all 0.05 because those additive tables cannot express the conjunction. Remaining errors are mostly window-first trials where the history is outside the window. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.65 (dev 0.64).

issues: Reproduced the claimed scores: dev 0.636 and test 0.653 R^2 beyond timing. Misses show no systematic error class. Mean error is about 0 in every phase, and the largest per-cell bias is about 0.001. The worst windows are mostly ones where the feature fires on the window's first trial, so the history it needs falls outside the window.

The 'grows about linearly to 0.5-0.7 by trials 98-99' claim overstates the shape. Fitting the core conjunction separately for each pair of ep_trial values gives 88-89: 0.03, 90-91: 0.10, 92-93: 0.26, 94-95: 0.41, 96-97: 0.44, 98-99: 0.42. The rise levels off at about 0.4 from trial 94 on, and the strongest single activations (about 0.6-0.7) are outliers, not the mean.
The ep_trial >= 90 cutoff is not quite strict. There is weak firing (about 0.03) at ep_trial 88-89.

The suppression from an earlier a2 is not limited to the trial three back. An a2 four trials back also strongly suppresses it (weight 0.06 vs 0.34 when trials 3 and 4 back were both a1). So it is better described as 'a run of a1 choices before the a1 S1 r trial'. Also, after a2 three back the drop is near-total if that a2 trial was rewarded (about 0) and partial if it was unrewarded (about 0.05).
The 2-back requirement checks out. Late a1 S2 r preceded by a1 S1 u, a1 S2 r/u or a2 gives about 0, while a1 S1 r gives about 0.31.
Belief: adding belief_lo inside the conjunction raises dev a little (0.678 to 0.685) but lowers test (0.684 to 0.682). The claim that belief adds nothing beyond history holds.
